entry.title: Together We Can Eliminate Cervical Cancer

media:group.media:title: Together We Can Eliminate Cervical Cancer
media:group.media:description:
World Cervical Cancer Day is marked on 17 November. To save lives and make #CervicalCancer history, we call on all countries to ensure that:
Every girl can get an HPV vaccine.
Every woman knows when she is due to be screened.
Every woman diagnosed receives the care she needs without delay.
Learn more:
https://www.who.int/campaigns/world-cervical-cancer-elimination-day/2026

entry.title: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) threatens our health, food security, economies and planet.

media:group.media:title: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) threatens our health, food security, economies and planet.
media:group.media:description:
#AntimicrobialResistance (AMR) threatens our health, food security, economies and planet.
To fight it, we must prevent infections, use antimicrobials responsibly, improve water, sanitation and hygiene, expand access to vaccines, diagnostics and treatments, and reduce pollution.
One Health, one action. Prevent AMR now.
Learn more about World AMR Awareness Week
https://www.who.int/campaigns/world-amr-awareness-week/world-amr-awareness-week-2026

entry.title: No child should die from the cold.

media:group.media:title: No child should die from the cold.
media:group.media:description:
For families in #Gaza who have already lost so much, a tent is often their only protection.
When it is gone, they are left exposed to the cold, to contaminated water and to disease.
At a press conference on 17 November 2026, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros highlighted the need for unobstructed and expedited entry at scale for shelter materials, clean water and sanitation supplies, medicines, vaccines and equipment to prevent hypothermia.
Watch the entire press conference:
https://www.youtube.com/live/9O1HRLnMx84?si=FbkG1-dK_zEVd_5c

entry.title: Strengthening Africa's health security: Dr Tedros' message to African Medicines Agency Week 2026

media:group.media:title: Strengthening Africa's health security: Dr Tedros' message to African Medicines Agency Week 2026
media:group.media:description: In a video message to the inaugural African Medicines Agency Week in Kigali, Rwanda, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus reaffirmed WHO’s commitment to strengthening regulatory systems across Africa. Highlighting progress made by national regulatory authorities and the importance of the WHO–African Medicines Agency partnership, he called for stronger regulatory cooperation, sustained investment and greater support for the Agency to accelerate access to safe, effective and quality-assured medical products, strengthen African manufacturing and advance health security across the continent.
